questions.question: Why is an int a poor type for a robot with four states?
options: It can hold four billion values, and the type asserts something false about the program
Integers are slower to compare than enums
An int cannot be used in a switch
Because states must be strings for logging
questions.explanation: Only a comment says which four values mean anything, and comments do not compile. A type that can hold exactly the four cannot be given a fifth.

questions.question: What does enum class give you that a plain enum does not?
options: Scoped names and no accidental conversion to a number
Faster comparisons
The ability to add values at runtime
Automatic conversion to a string
questions.explanation: A plain enum converts to int freely, which lets through comparing against a raw number and passing a state where a count was expected.

questions.question: Why leave the default label off a switch over an enum?
options: So the compiler warns when a value is added and this switch has not been updated
Because default is not allowed with enum class
To make the switch faster
Because every case is always handled anyway
questions.explanation: Adding default silences that warning forever, trading a message today for a bug later. Put the fallback after the switch instead.

questions.question: Why does a faulted robot ignore every event except a reset?
options: Recovery must be a decision somebody makes, not something a stale command can cause
Because a faulted robot cannot receive events
To keep the transition table smaller
Because faults clear themselves after a timeout
questions.explanation: It is the watchdog principle from lesson 14-02: the safe state is the one you stay in until a human deliberately leaves it.

questions.question: Why is one enum better than three booleans for a state?
options: Three booleans give eight combinations and most of them are nonsense that nothing prevents
Booleans use more memory
Booleans cannot be switched on
There is no difference, it is a style choice
questions.explanation: is_moving and is_stopped can both be true at once. A single enum plus one transition function cannot represent a contradiction.

questions.question: Where else in this curriculum have you already met this pattern?
options: ConfigError, TickQuality and ReadError, each a closed set of possibilities
Only in this lesson
In the test framework's macros
In the build system's dependency graph
questions.explanation: A closed set of reasons something failed is the same idea as a closed set of states, and it is everywhere in robot code once you see it.
